methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $117M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
VEIR, a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Tim Heidel, has raised $117M to date. Valuation analysis draws on two methodologies triangulated against a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M), alongside a broader comp universe of 9 private and 1 public firm in the climate-tech sector.

Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 1.9x multiplier to the $117M capital raised proxy, implying a valuation of $222M. Peer-median methodology across the three closest comparables yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with an observed range of $700M to $3.0B. The dispersion reflects meaningful variation in technology maturity and market positioning within the sector at the Series C level.

Triangulating both methods yields a valuation range of $189M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $611M. The wide range reflects two competing signals: stage-progression suggests VEIR remains in the low-to-mid hundreds of millions, while peer medians—drawn from more mature Series C firms—point toward substantially higher valuations. Key uncertainties include VEIR's specific technology differentiation relative to peers, revenue trajectory, and path to next-stage funding. Resolution of these factors will be critical to narrowing the range.
